newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WEBSTER SHRUGS OFF INJURY TO SEIZE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WEBSTER SHRUGS OFF INJURY TO SEIZE LEAD.

text.p: Englishman Steve Webster shrugged off a thumb injury to shoot a 66, only one stroke off the course record, for a one-shot lead in the European Grand Prix opening round on Thursday.

Webster trapped his left thumb in his car door at the weekend after returning home from the Tournament Players Championship in Hamburg but decided to play after a painful four days without being able to hit a ball.

Playing through his pain he finished one stroke ahead of Ireland's Padraig Harrington, who was wearing contact lenses in a tournament for the first time, and a surprise challenger, Sweden's little-known Fredrik Andersson.
Spaniard Juan Carlos Pinero bogeyed his last two holes for a 68. Also on four-under were Italian Emanuele Canonica, another Swede, Mats Hallberg and another Englishman, Steven Bottomley.

Europe's number one for the past four years, Colin Montgomerie of Scotland, began his bid for a first win of the year with a 69, picking up three birdies in his first six holes to also put himself in great heart for next week's U.S. Open, but then found his putting faded.
In the group on three-under, too, was the defending champion Retief Goosen of South Africa.

Webster, the 1995 European Tour qualifying school winner after being top amateur in that year's British Open, but who then lost his card and had to requalify last year, fashioned his lead with an eagle and six birdies, also running up two bogeys.
"The thumb was so painful I didn't think I'd be able to play," said Webster. "I couldn't hit a ball for four days and played only nine holes practice before deciding to try to get round.."
